standards.title: Send Feedback in the app

checks.problem: app-release.config.json has no valid feedback.email
no app source file carries the marker comment `app-standard: feedback`
the marked file opens no mail composer (MFMailComposeViewController or a mailto: URL)
the marked file does not build the subject `[<App name> feedback] <version> (<build>)`
no control is labelled exactly `Send Feedback`
the address in feedback.email appears nowhere in the app source
the marked file is in the repository but no screen uses it
this Kids Category app shows the control where no parental gate is evident

standards.fix: Copy assets/feedback/FeedbackButton.swift (native) or assets/feedback/feedback.ts (Expo, React Native, Capacitor) into the app, put the control on the settings or about screen, set feedback.email in app-release.config.json and mention the address on the support page.
standards.verify: On a simulator or device, tap Send Feedback and see the composer or the fallback with the right address, subject and footer; open the support page and see the same address.

standards.title: Privacy policy linked inside the app

checks.problem: no link to the privacy policy found in the app source
listing.privacyPolicyUrl is the same page as the marketing or support URL; App Review needs a page that is the privacy policy

standards.fix: Publish the privacy policy (the store data's listing.privacyPolicyUrl) as its own page, not the marketing or support page, and link it from the settings or about screen, behind the parental gate in a Kids Category app. Where the app builds the URL in a way the audit cannot see, add the comment `app-standard: privacy-link` beside it.
standards.verify: On a simulator or device, open the link from inside the app and see the live policy.

standards.title: Support page linked inside the app

checks.problem: no link to the support page found in the app source

standards.fix: Link the support page (the store data's listing.supportUrl) from the settings or about screen, behind the parental gate in a Kids Category app. Where the app builds the URL in a way the audit cannot see, add the comment `app-standard: support-link` beside it.
standards.verify: On a simulator or device, open the link from inside the app and see the live support page.

standards.title: Embedded web pages sell nothing

checks.problem: the app embeds a web view, and no source file carries the marker comment `app-standard: web-sheet` beside the code that limits what it shows
the marked file sets no navigation policy, so any link on the page opens inside the app
the marked file never refuses or hides pricing, subscription, upgrade or checkout pages

standards.fix: Limit every web view to the job it is there for (signing in, a privacy page): refuse links to pages outside that job rather than opening them; refuse pricing, upgrade, subscription and checkout pages even on allowed hosts; cover any other page with the app's own screen; and hide any part of an allowed page that shows prices or plans, which sign-in pages now do. Put the comment `app-standard: web-sheet` in the file that does this, with tests that replay the page App Review would reach. Plenty's SignInPolicy.swift is a worked example.
standards.verify: Open each web view on a simulator, scroll every allowed page to the bottom and tap each link that is not part of the job: no price, plan, subscription or upgrade offer appears and nothing else opens.

standards.title: Ask for a rating in the app

checks.problem: no app source file carries the marker comment `app-standard: rating`
the marked file never reaches the store's own rating prompt (requestReview, StoreReview or InAppReview)
the marked file does not carry the shared rule (good moments, days, and the wait between asks)
the marked file is in the repository but nothing calls it after a good moment
this Kids Category app asks for a rating where no parental gate is evident

standards.fix: Copy assets/rating/RatingPrompt.swift (native) or assets/rating/rating.ts (Expo, React Native, Capacitor) into the app and call it right after the app's good moment (references/standards.md, Ask for a rating): `if RatingPrompt.goodMoment() { requestReview() }` in SwiftUI, RatingPrompt.askIfDue() elsewhere, ratingGoodMoment(version, platform) in TypeScript. In a Kids Category app call it only behind the parental gate. Test the app's own call site where the app has tests.
standards.verify: In a debug build on a simulator, reach the good moment three times across two days (move the device date, or seed the stored state in a UI test) and see the system rating prompt once; reach it again and see nothing. Read the stored state back: the count restarted and the version is recorded.

standards.title: More apps row in the app

checks.problem: no app source file carries the marker comment `app-standard: more-apps`
the marked file opens no App Store page (https://apps.apple.com/app/id<id>)
no generated list carries the marker `app-standard catalogue: more-apps`; write it with scripts/more-apps.mjs
the marked file is in the repository but no screen shows the row

standards.fix: Copy assets/more-apps/MoreApps.swift (native) or assets/more-apps/moreApps.ts (Expo, React Native, Capacitor) into the app unchanged, write the list beside it with `node $S/more-apps.mjs write --swift <folder>/MoreAppsCatalog.swift` (or `--ts <folder>/moreAppsCatalog.ts`) from the app repository, and show the row on the settings or about screen near Send Feedback (MoreAppsSection or MoreAppsLink in SwiftUI; moreAppsFor(platform, bundleId) drawn with the app's own rows elsewhere). iOS only: hide it on Android and the web. When the audit says the list is out of date, run the same write again in this run's build.
standards.verify: On a simulator, open the settings or about screen, see the More apps row with every listed app's icon, name and line and not this app, tap one and see its App Store page open (a simulator without the App Store app shows the page in Safari).

standards.title: First-launch count

checks.problem: no app source file carries the marker comment `app-standard: first-launch`
the marked file does not send to the owner's endpoint https://astrojams-apps.vercel.app/api/launch
the marked file reads or makes an identifier; the event carries only app, version, platform and channel
the marked file is in the repository but nothing calls it when the app starts
no privacy manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy, or an Expo config's ios.privacyManifests) declares Product Interaction collected for Analytics

standards.fix: Copy assets/first-launch/FirstLaunch.swift (native, and Capacitor apps from their AppDelegate) or assets/first-launch/firstLaunch.ts (Expo, React Native) into the app unchanged and call it once at startup with the app's catalogue id (marketing/apps/<id>.json in app-sites): `.task { FirstLaunch.report(app: "<id>") }` on the root view, `FirstLaunch.report(app:)` in didFinishLaunching, or reportFirstLaunch('<id>', platform) in a startup effect. Declare Product Interaction (not linked, not tracking, Analytics) in the app's privacy manifest, say it in the privacy policy, and record the App Privacy change for App Store Connect (references/standards.md).
standards.verify: Launch a build with -firstLaunchSend on a simulator: one POST reaches /api/launch (the endpoint answers 204) and `marketing.mjs launches` shows it under debug; relaunch and see no second request. Read the privacy manifest in the built app and the live privacy policy.
